column1: # config/secret-patterns.tsv - the team's single source of secret and private-data patterns (Issue #15).
# Generated copies (never edit them; run python scripts/generate_runtime.py):
#   skills/development/scripts/secret-patterns.tsv         secret_scan.py and the scripts that use it
# Columns, separated by one TAB: id, scope, flags, regex.
#   scope  secret   never in files, commits, pushes, commands or anything published
#          private  never in text published to GitHub (Issues, Pull Requests, comments, reviews, commit
#                   messages); allowed in code, where emails or paths can be legitimate
#          allow    a match of a non-strict rule is ignored when the matched text also matches this regex
#          strict   the allow list never applies (high-confidence provider formats)
#          luhn     the digits of the match must pass the Luhn check (card numbers)
#          secret / private   (allow rules only) the scope the allow rule applies to; none means both
# Regex dialect: the subset shared by POSIX ERE (grep -E), JavaScript and Python. No \b, \d, \s, \w,
# lookarounds, lazy quantifiers or non-capturing groups; a backslash inside [] is literal in ERE.
# Tests and examples must use obviously fake values (containing test, fake, dummy, example, sample, mock
# or changeme) or placeholders such as <token> and ${TOKEN}; secrets in tests are built by concatenation.
